## Key finding: CM on join keys blocks the BF

- q05: plan identical with CM on/off; lineitem scan 0.9s CPU with BF.

- FSST DecompressVector path: enable_fsst_vectors is off by default, so it is not hot. No dict_fsst segments.
- HJ prefetch, agg run-collapse, in-place finalize, FSST heap reuse, dictionary filter, scan filter cost ordering, early HT grow, sparse perfect HJ, bitpacking select, BF on sparse perfect HJ: ~0% or worse.
- Large perfect HA: real q13 gain, but the official bench flags q18 each time (DEAD).
- E0010 distinct HT partitioned on group hash (q16 -7.4%), E0008 exact BF through CM offset (-3.9%): retired; superseded if CM key compression goes.

1. Aggregate CM skip for q13 (filed), once E0017 lands.

3. q18 IN-list optional filter → evaluate per row when the key set is small (12M→~800 rows), small gain.
4. q04/q08/q07 not analysed yet (each about 7% of total). Profile q04 and q08 next.

- CM: src/optimizer/compressed_materialization.cpp dispatches to compressed_materialization/compress_{aggregate,comparison_join,distinct,order}.cpp. Join key compression is the probe_compress_bindings block in CompressComparisonJoin.
- Rule registration order: src/optimizer/optimizer.cpp. Scan-filter cardinality: RelationStatisticsHelper::InspectTableFilter.

- OptionalFilter is zonemap only. SelectivityOptionalFilter evaluates rows (the BF uses it); key-set ranges and IN-list are plain OptionalFilter.
- BF gate: CanUseBloomFilter (physical_hash_join.cpp ~865). build_side_has_filter is set in join_filter_pushdown_optimizer.cpp ~331. Exact BF: TrySetExactBloomFilter, 128 bits/key cap.
- Perfect HJ: perfect_hash_join_executor.cpp CanDoPerfectHashJoin. Perfect HA: plan_aggregate.cpp.
- FSST scan decode: src/storage/compression/fsst.cpp FSSTScanState::DecompressStrings.

- Testing BF: compare against SET disabled_optimizers='join_filter_pushdown'.
- Budget is tight (~$4/session): read memory, the ledger tail and the profile head, then dispatch.

issues.title: Rerun: Stop compressing hash-join keys in compressed materialization
issues.hypothesis: E0017 was retired at +0.6% visible geomean, but the harness itself listed q09 and q19 as faster beyond noise and nothing as slower beyond noise. The implementer measured q09 at -7..-19% over 5 runs and q03 at -11.6% on the last full run (geomean -4.8%). The mechanism is confirmed in the profile: physical_hash_join.cpp ~1059 builds a BF only when storage_offset.IsNull(). A probe key under a CM compress projection gets an offset, so the orders scan in q09 and the lineitem scan in q03 never get the BF (raw q09 with CM disabled: 542→335ms, orders scan 15M→2.94M rows). The bench swings ±20% per template on identical code, so the retirement looks like noise. Untouched templates (q19 -17% on an unchanged tree) confirm how noisy it is.
issues.plan: Reapply E0017 exactly. In CompressedMaterialization::CompressComparisonJoin (src/optimizer/compressed_materialization/compress_comparison_join.cpp), remove the block that compresses both columns of a single equality condition generically and adds the probe key to probe_compress_bindings. All conditions then go through GetReferencedBindings, so join keys are never compressed. Build-side payload compression and aggregate/order/distinct CM stay unchanged. Check with EXPLAIN that q09's orders scan and q03's lineitem scan show a BF. Run the bench at least twice and report per-template medians.
issues.generality: Any hash join whose probe key would have been compressed by CM, which is every single-equality integer join feeding a materializing operator. All of them regain BF pushdown into the probe scan. Joins with a big build side lose a little memory saving from narrower keys. q13 adds an aggregate compress projection above the join (~0.58s CPU), so it could be slightly slower.
issues.risk: Low. It removes an optimization and touches no execution code, and it was already verified correct on all templates with hidden validation ok. The main risk is bench noise.

issues.title: Skip aggregate CM compress on group keys from large join outputs with perfect HA
issues.hypothesis: After E0017, q13 gets a 15M-row __internal_compress projection (~0.58s CPU) above the RIGHT perfect HJ, feeding a perfect hash aggregate on c_custkey. The perfect HA already uses the stats range, so compressing the key to a narrower type gains nothing but costs a full pass over 15M rows.
issues.plan: In src/optimizer/compressed_materialization/compress_aggregate.cpp, skip compressing a group column when the aggregate's group count is small relative to its input. Alternatively, skip it when the group key is an integer whose stats range fits the perfect-HA bit budget, because the HA then does not materialize wide keys. First measure on q13 with E0017 applied: compare compress-projection CPU against SET disabled_optimizers='compressed_materialization'.
issues.generality: Aggregates over large join outputs on integer keys with a small range. These are common for GROUP BY on FK keys.
issues.risk: Low-medium. Aggregates that materialize many groups could use more memory.
